messages:
maya: FYI ACME reported a sharp increase in 429s on their Dedicated cluster overnight, saying requests started failing around 02:10 UTC. They see high tail latency too.
samir: Can you paste the error examples and any kv eviction logs? 429s could be the throttle layer reacting to heavy KV eviction churn.
maya: Customer logs: \n
```
2025-08-12T01:58:21Z evict: tenant=acme ctx=long-ctx keycount=824567 evicted=1024 reason=kv_pressure
2025-08-12T01:58:21Z kv_cache: occupancy=96% frag=0.67 free_chunks=4
2025-08-12T02:10:03Z throttle=token_bucket drop=1 route=/v1/generate tenant=acme
```
maya: They also ran a few long-context batches (30k tokens) for a re-ranking job.
jen: That frag=0.67 number is telling. We saw similar memory fragmentation when many large contexts were pinned and then freed sporadically. It prevents contiguous allocation so eviction churn spikes.
alvin: Ops note: autoscaler logs show a backoff at 02:05 due to quota limits in the region, so we didn't add nodes before the surge finished. ops-bot: autoscaler_event: cluster=dedicated-us-east-2 action=backoff reason=quota_limit timestamp=2025-08-12T02:05:12Z
samir: Ok. Repro steps request for SRE: can we get the customer to run a minimal repro? e.g. two curl calls in parallel to simulate long-context hit: \n
```
# generate two long prompts concurrently
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"rwd-long-30k","input":"<30k tokens>"}' &
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"rwd-long-30k","input":"<30k tokens>"}' &
```
maya: Customer already ran a similar load but I'll ask them to run the exact pair of commands and collect `/internal/metrics/kv_mem_stats` output.
jen: Short-term mitigations: 1) bump the dedicated pool by 2 nodes for ACME (stop-gap) 2) enable kv_compaction=true on their tenant config to trigger background compaction 3) temporarily set route-level per-tenant token rate limit lower for heavy long-context routes to reduce burst.
alvin: Config note: we can toggle `kv_compaction` via the customer feature flag API. Also we can uplift `reserved_kv_bytes` for their tenant to avoid immediate eviction.
samir: Also check model fallback policy — if we route large contexts to quantized variants with smaller KV footprint it can help. But that affects quality.
maya: Customer is asking for concrete next steps and timeline. I'll propose: scale +2 nodes now, enable compaction, collect kv_mem_stats, and run repro. ETA to customer: 2 hours to scale and enable flag. :hourglass:
jen: Longer-term: we should schedule a defrag job on the serving runtime (low-priority background compaction) and add fragmentation alerting (frag > 0.6 + occupancy > 90%). Put this on eng-runtime backlog.
samir: Action items: maya owner -> ask customer to run repro + share metrics; alvin owner -> flip kv_compaction and bump reserved_kv_bytes for acme; jen owner -> add frag alert + run node scale now; samir -> follow for model fallback policy adjustments.
maya: I'll update the customer and send repro instructions. tagging @alvin @jen to proceed with infra ops. :spiral_notepad:
ops-bot: ticket_created: #INC-2025-4987 owner=maya severity=high category=kv-pressure
maya: Thanks team, will post updates here after repro results.
